es.summary: Infección viral que causa inflamación aguda o crónica del hígado. Puede progresar a cirrosis o carcinoma hepatocelular.
key_points: Transmisión por sangre, semen y fluidos corporales.
ALT/AST elevados > 2 veces el límite superior normal.
Vacuna disponible y recomendada para contactos y recién nacidos.
Tratamiento antiviral de primera línea: tenofovir o entecavir.

pathophysiology: El virus HBV penetra hepatocitos y replica su ADN.
La respuesta inmune causa necrosis y necroinflamación hepática.
Daño crónico lleva a fibrosis, cirrosis y posible carcinoma.
risk_factors: Exposición perinatal a madre HBsAg positiva.
Uso de drogas intravenosas o compartir agujas.
Relaciones sexuales sin protección con portador.
treatment: Manejo de complicaciones: diuréticos, trasplante hepático.
Vacunación a contactos y recién nacidos.
complications: Coagulopatía por disminución de factores de coagulación.
nursing_care: Evaluar ictericia, nivel de energía y dolor abdominal.
Monitorear ALT, AST, bilirrubina y carga viral.
Controlar signos vitales y balance hídrico.
Aplicar precauciones estándar y aislamiento por sangre.
patient_teaching: Importancia de la vacunación y completar esquema.
Evitar compartir objetos punzocortantes y usar preservativo.
Cumplir con la terapia antiviral y citas de laboratorio.
Reconocer signos de alarma: sangrado, aumento de ictericia.

outcomes: Nivel de energía: alcanzar 4/5 en escala de 0‑5 en 48 h
Participación en actividades de autocuidado: 80 % de cumplimiento en 3 días

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de fatiga usando escala de Borg cada turno
interventions.rationale: Permite cuantificar la fatiga y medir respuesta a intervenciones

interventions.action: Programar períodos de descanso y sueño adecuados
interventions.rationale: Reduce la demanda energética y favorece la recuperación hepática

interventions.action: Fomentar actividades de bajo consumo energético, como caminatas cortas
interventions.rationale: Mantiene movilidad sin sobrecargar al paciente

interventions.action: Ofrecer alimentos ricos en proteínas y calorías según tolerancia
interventions.rationale: Apoya la reparación hepática y mejora la energía

interventions.action: Monitorear resultados de laboratorio (ALT, AST, HBV DNA) semanalmente
interventions.rationale: Correlaciona la carga viral con la intensidad de la fatiga

outcomes: No se presentarán nuevas infecciones transmisibles durante la hospitalización
Paciente demostrará correcta técnica de higiene de manos en 100 % de oportunidades

interventions.action: Enseñar y practicar la técnica de lavado de manos antes y después de cada procedimiento
interventions.rationale: Reduce la transmisión de HBV y otras infecciones

interventions.action: Aplicar guantes y barreras de protección al manipular sangre o fluidos
interventions.rationale: Previene exposición directa al virus

interventions.action: Educar sobre no compartir objetos punzocortantes y uso de jeringas estériles
interventions.rationale: Disminuye la vía de transmisión percutánea

interventions.action: Informar sobre la importancia del uso de preservativo en relaciones sexuales
interventions.rationale: Reduce transmisión sexual del virus

interventions.action: Coordinar vacunación contra hepatitis B para contactos susceptibles
interventions.rationale: Proporciona inmunidad activa y previene nuevas infecciones

en.summary: Viral infection that causes acute or chronic inflammation of the liver. It can progress to cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma.
key_points: Transmission by blood, semen, and bodily fluids.
ALT/AST elevated > 2 times the upper normal limit.
Vaccination available and recommended for contacts and newborns.
First‑line antiviral treatment: tenofovir or entecavir.

pathophysiology: HBV virus penetrates hepatocytes and replicates its DNA.
The immune response causes hepatic necrosis and necroinflammation.
Chronic damage leads to fibrosis, cirrhosis, and possible carcinoma.
risk_factors: Intravenous drug use or sharing needles.
Unprotected sexual contact with a carrier.
signs_symptoms: Mild fever in the acute phase.
treatment: Management of complications: diuretics, liver transplant.
complications: Coagulopathy due to decreased clotting factors.
nursing_care: Assess jaundice, energy level, and abdominal pain.
Monitor ALT, AST, bilirubin, and viral load.
Track vital signs and fluid balance.
Apply standard precautions and blood isolation.
patient_teaching: Importance of vaccination and completing the schedule.
Avoid sharing sharps and use condoms.
Adhere to antiviral therapy and lab appointments.
Recognize warning signs: bleeding, increased jaundice.

outcomes: Energy level: reach 4/5 on 0‑5 scale within 48 h
Participation in self‑care activities: 80 % compliance in 3 days

interventions.action: Assess fatigue level using Borg scale each shift
interventions.rationale: Quantifies fatigue and measures response to interventions

interventions.action: Schedule adequate rest and sleep periods
interventions.rationale: Reduces energy demand and promotes hepatic recovery

interventions.action: Encourage low‑energy activities, such as short walks
interventions.rationale: Maintains mobility without overloading the patient

interventions.action: Offer protein‑rich and caloric foods as tolerated
interventions.rationale: Supports hepatic repair and improves energy

interventions.action: Monitor laboratory results (ALT, AST, HBV DNA) weekly
interventions.rationale: Correlates viral load with fatigue intensity

outcomes: No new transmissible infections will occur during hospitalization
Patient will demonstrate proper hand‑washing technique 100 % of the time

interventions.action: Teach and practice hand‑washing technique before and after each procedure
interventions.rationale: Reduces transmission of HBV and other infections

interventions.action: Apply gloves and protective barriers when handling blood or fluids
interventions.rationale: Prevents direct exposure to the virus

interventions.action: Educate about not sharing sharps and using sterile syringes
interventions.rationale: Reduces percutaneous transmission route

interventions.action: Inform about the importance of condom use in sexual relationships
interventions.rationale: Reduces sexual transmission of the virus

interventions.action: Coordinate hepatitis B vaccination for susceptible contacts
interventions.rationale: Provides active immunity and prevents new infections

summary.0.quote: Hepatitis A condition characterized by inflammation of the liver, hepatitis is often the result of a viral infection (WHO, 2019).

summary.1.quote: Hepatitis B virus infection can lead to serious complications, including the development of cirrhosis of the liver, liver disease, hepatocellular carcinoma, and death.

key_points.0.quote: The virus spreads through contact with blood, semen, or other body fluids from a person who has the virus.

key_points.1.quote: Positive HBsAg Acute or chronic infection

key_points.3.quote: Vaccination is available and is recommended for children as part of the standard vaccination schedule (one dose at birth and the second by 18 months of age) and for adults at greater risk (e.g., those with certain diseases, IV-drug users, those who have sex with multiple partners).

sections.pathophysiology.2.quote: Hepatitis B virus infection can lead to serious complications, including the development of cirrhosis of the liver, liver disease, hepatocellular carcinoma, and death.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: All pregnant persons should be tested for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and high-risk patients should be tested again at delivery so that the infant can be treated right after birth (CDC, 2021a).

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: You can also reduce your chance of hepatitis B infection by: Not sharing drug needles or other drug materials

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: HBV can be spread through blood and body fluids, perinatally; percutaneously, such as in intravenous drug use; and through sexual contact (Lok, 2023).

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Yellowish eyes and skin, called jaundice

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: These symptoms can include: Dark yellow urine Diarrhea Fatigue Fever Gray- or clay-colored stools Joint pain Loss of appetite Nausea and/or vomiting Abdominal pain Yellowish eyes and skin, called jaundice If you have chronic hepatitis B, you may not have symptoms until complications develop.
